from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Ternary systems use three digits: zero, one, two.",
            "They represent choices, not just simple quantities.",
            "Three bits create twenty-seven distinct states.",
            "Think of buttons defining a coordinate system.",
            "This structure builds our foundation for logic."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Ternary Foundation", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Ternary systems use three digits: zero, one, two.
        c1 = Circle(radius=0.5, color="#E63946")
        c2 = Circle(radius=0.5, color="#E63946")
        c3 = Circle(radius=0.5, color="#E63946")
        VGroup(c1, c2, c3).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        self.place_at_grid(VGroup(c1, c2, c3), 'B2', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.play(Create(c1), Create(c2), Create(c3))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#E63946"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # They represent choices, not just simple quantities.
        l0 = Text("0", color=WHITE).move_to(c1.get_center())
        l1 = Text("1", color=WHITE).move_to(c2.get_center())
        l2 = Text("2", color=WHITE).move_to(c3.get_center())
        self.play(Write(l0), Write(l1), Write(l2))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#A8DADC"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Three bits create twenty-seven distinct states.
        disks = VGroup(
            Circle(radius=0.5, color="#457B9D", fill_opacity=1),
            Circle(radius=0.5, color="#457B9D", fill_opacity=1),
            Circle(radius=0.5, color="#457B9D", fill_opacity=1)
        ).arrange(DOWN, buff=-0.2)
        self.place_at_grid(disks, 'D4', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Transform(VGroup(c1, c2, c3), disks))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#F1FAEE"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Think of buttons defining a coordinate system.
        coord_label = Text("(x, y, z)", color="#F1FAEE", font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(coord_label, 'D2', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(coord_label))
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#F1FAEE"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # This structure builds our foundation for logic.
        self.play(FadeIn(Rectangle(width=3, height=2, color="#457B9D", fill_opacity=0.2).move_to(disks.get_center())))
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#A8DADC"))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [

            "Each move adds one to the state.",

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(pegs))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#F1FAEE")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        state_text = MathTex("000_3 \\rightarrow 001_3").scale(0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(state_text, "D3")

        self.lecture[1].set_color("#A8DADC")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#F1FAEE")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        path = NumberLine(x_range=[0, 3, 1], length=4)

        self.place_at_grid(path, "E3")

        self.lecture[3].set_color("#A8DADC")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#F1FAEE")

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Now, map these moves to two dimensions.", "The path traces a Sierpinski triangle.", "Each disk expansion grows the fractal.", "Anchor points guide the pattern's evolution.", "The entire graph reveals the geometry."]
        self.setup_layout("Mapping the Sierpinski Triangle", lecture_lines)

        # Define colors
        color_main = "#457B9D"
        color_fill = "#1D3557"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        triangle = Polygon(UP * 2, LEFT * 2 + DOWN * 1.5, RIGHT * 2 + DOWN * 1.5, color=color_main)
        self.place_at_grid(triangle, 'C3', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Create(triangle))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        # Subdivide
        t1 = triangle.copy()
        t1.scale(0.5)
        self.play(triangle.animate.set_opacity(0.3))
        # Keep it simple for now
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        # Fill inner triangle
        inner = Triangle(color=color_fill, fill_opacity=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(inner, 'C3', scale_factor=0.3)
        self.play(FadeIn(inner))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        # Anchor points
        dots = VGroup(*[Dot(color=RED) for _ in range(3)])
        # Position at triangle vertices
        self.place_at_grid(dots[0], 'A3', scale_factor=1)
        self.place_at_grid(dots[1], 'E1', scale_factor=1)
        self.place_at_grid(dots[2], 'E5', scale_factor=1)
        self.play(LaggedStart(*[GrowFromCenter(d) for d in dots]))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Ternary numbers are our fractal GPS.",
            "They locate vertices within the structure.",
            "The graph represents the total state-space.",
            "Logic and geometry unify perfectly here.",
            "This concludes our hidden geometry exploration."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Synthesis: The Deep Connection", lecture_lines)
        
        # Sierpinski Triangle (simplified)
        def get_sierpinski(order=2):
            points = [UP * 2, LEFT * 2 + DOWN * 2, RIGHT * 2 + DOWN * 2]
            if order == 0:
                return Polygon(*points)
            
            # Simple recursive visual
            vgroup = VGroup()
            # This is a placeholder for the actual structure
            triangle = Polygon(*points, color=BLUE_D)
            vgroup.add(triangle)
            return vgroup

        sierpinski = get_sierpinski()
        self.place_at_grid(sierpinski, 'C3', scale_factor=0.6)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#8ECAE6"))
        gps_label = Text("Ternary: (1, 0, 2)", color="#8ECAE6", font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(gps_label, 'A3')
        self.play(FadeIn(gps_label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFB703"))
        target_dot = Dot(color="#FFB703").move_to(sierpinski.get_center() + RIGHT * 0.5 + UP * 0.2)
        self.play(Create(target_dot))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FB8500"))
        state_space_box = Rectangle(color="#FB8500", width=2, height=2)
        self.place_at_grid(state_space_box, 'E3')
        self.play(Create(state_space_box))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#219EBC"))
        self.play(
            sierpinski.animate.set_color("#219EBC"),
            state_space_box.animate.set_color("#219EBC")
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Hidden Geometry of Counting: From Ternary Systems to Fractals
outline.target_audience: University students (Computer Science or Mathematics majors)

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Ternary Foundation
sections.content: Introduce base-3 counting (0, 1, 2) as a language of 'choice' rather than 'quantity'. Use a branching tree diagram to show how 3 bits represent 27 states (3^3), setting the stage for 3-peg logic.
sections.example: A smart lock with 3 buttons (A, B, C) where each press changes the state; show how 3 buttons represent positions in a 3-dimensional coordinate system.

sections.title: The Constrained Towers of Hanoi
sections.content: Explain the variation where disks can only move between adjacent pegs (A↔B, B↔C). Connect the movement to the ternary system: each disk state transition requires a specific base-3 increment. Visualize this as a path on a line.
sections.example: Representing the state of 3 disks as a 3-digit ternary number (e.g., 000 to 222), where each valid move adds 1 in 'ternary arithmetic'.

sections.title: Mapping the Sierpinski Triangle
sections.content: Transition from the 1D path of Hanoi moves to a 2D graph. Demonstrate that the sequence of allowed moves in the constrained Hanoi problem perfectly traces the edges of a Sierpinski triangle. Use an animation showing the path 'growing' as more disks are added.
sections.example: A spider crawling between three anchor points; as it visits every possible sub-triangle, its path recreates the Sierpinski fractal pattern.

sections.title: Synthesis: The Deep Connection
sections.content: Conclude by unifying the concepts: The Sierpinski graph represents the state-space of the constrained Towers of Hanoi, and ternary numbers serve as the 'GPS coordinates' to locate any point within that fractal structure.
sections.example: A visual overlay: showing a ternary coordinate (1, 0, 2) and highlighting the exact corresponding vertex within a 3rd-order Sierpinski triangle.
